overall.sentence: Nanoscale SQUID imaging of orbital magnetism in rhombohedral graphene was already reported for the tetralayer quarter metal (2503.14146, cited as [44]) and, two weeks before this paper, for the superconducting state of pentalayer (2605.13303, cited as [34]); what this paper adds is the 3 to 15 layer survey, the finite-density ring-of-fire peak, the density-driven sign change and gate reversal of the whole device, and the 0.1 μB per carrier bound.

assessment.claim: 1: magnetization of the quarter metal peaks at finite density in 3 to 15 layer devices, attributed to the Berry ring of fire
assessment.note: nanoSQUID imaging of the tetralayer quarter metal (cited [44]) and local magnetometry of the trilayer (2310.03781, cited [29]) match system and method; the multi-thickness survey and the finite-density peak tied to the ring of fire are new in the question.

assessment.claim: 2: the superconducting state of a tetralayer carries a finite orbital moment (valley polarization in the superconductor)
assessment.note: Dutta et al., posted 13 May 2026 before this paper, image isospin domains with SQUID-on-tip in rhombohedral pentalayer and report magnetic evidence of time-reversal breaking in the superconductor; only the layer number differs (5 vs 4), and the paper mentions it only in a Note added.

assessment.claim: Intro: 'experimental studies to date have been limited to the electronic transport response' for the chiral superconductor
assessment.note: The cited [34] is a magnetic-imaging study of the same kind of superconductor posted earlier, so the statement does not hold as worded.

assessment.claim: 3: stochastic resistance switching arises from a density-tuned sign change of the valley magnetization that creates metastable domains
assessment.note: Dutta et al. link transport regimes of the superconductor to chiral domains with resistive walls, and Grover et al. (2201.06901, cited [20]) image density-driven K to K' flips forming valley domains in magic-angle graphene; the sign-change mechanism in rhombohedral graphene, in metal and superconductor, is new.

assessment.claim: 4: 'first real-space imaging' of electrically controlled (capacitive) magnetization reversal
assessment.note: Grover et al. (cited [20]) imaged with SQUID-on-tip density-driven recondensation from K to K' that flips the local Chern number and magnetization in moire graphene; the claim as worded is not restricted to rhombohedral graphene, where whole-device gate reversal is new.

assessment.claim: 5: condensation magnetization at the superconducting transition bounded at 0.1 μB per carrier
assessment.note: No earlier quantitative bound found; Dutta et al. detect time-reversal breaking thermodynamically in the superconductor and Zhang et al. (2603.25807, cited [24]) image the Meissner response of a nonmagnetic rhombohedral superconductor; only one query targeted this claim, so it is not graded no_precedent_found.

positioning: The paper extends nanoSQUID magnetometry of rhombohedral graphene, previously done on the trilayer (2310.03781) and tetralayer (2503.14146) quarter metal, to a 3 to 15 layer series, and adds the finite-density magnetization peak, the gate-driven sign change and whole-device reversal, and a quantitative bound on condensation magnetization. Its closest competitor is Dutta et al. (2605.13303), posted two weeks earlier, which images chiral domains in the pentalayer superconductor with the same technique and also links switching to domains; the paper acknowledges it only in a Note added, and two statements (transport-only prior work, first imaging of gate reversal) need rewording against [34] and [20]. A transport study of gate-toggled orbital magnetism in rhombohedral hexalayer graphene (2509.24672) is not cited.

issues.claim: Prior experiments on the chiral superconductor were transport-only.
issues.headline: Cited preprint [34] already imaged magnetism in this superconductor
issues.issue: The introduction says experiments on the chiral superconductor have been limited to transport, but Dutta et al. (arXiv:2605.13303, cited as [34]), posted before this paper, used SQUID-on-tip imaging to detect time-reversal breaking and chiral domains in the rhombohedral pentalayer superconductor. The paper mentions that work only in a Note added, so the introduction and the headline claim read as if it did not exist.

evidence.quote: However, experimental studies to date have been limited to the electronic transport response, which is dominated by the zero resistance of the superconducting state.

issues.fix: Reword the sentence to acknowledge [34] and state what this work adds against it (tetralayer, density-resolved moment, the 0.1 μB bound, the sign-change mechanism); move the comparison from the Note added into the main text.

edit.before: However, experimental studies to date have been limited to the electronic transport response, which is dominated by the zero resistance of the superconducting state.
edit.after: Until recently, experimental studies have been limited to the electronic transport response, which is dominated by the zero resistance of the superconducting state; nanoSQUID imaging of rhombohedral pentalayer graphene has now reported magnetic evidence of time-reversal symmetry breaking in the superconductor [34].

issues.claim: First real-space imaging of electrically controlled magnetization reversal.
issues.headline: First imaging of gate-driven reversal contradicted by cited Ref. 20
issues.issue: Grover et al. (arXiv:2201.06901, cited as [20]) imaged with SQUID-on-tip how filling the band drives electrons from valley K to K', flipping the local Chern number and orbital magnetization in magic-angle graphene. The 'first real-space imaging' claim is not restricted to rhombohedral graphene, so as worded it is contradicted by a paper in this reference list.

evidence.quote: Our results here represent the first real-space imaging of this unique orbital magnetic phenomenon, and demonstrate that it is a generic feature of metallic orbital ferromagnets in rhombohedral graphene across a wide range of layer numbers
evidence.location: Capacitively driven domain reversal, end of section

issues.fix: Restrict the priority claim to what is new (whole-device gate reversal in metallic rhombohedral orbital magnets across layer numbers) and position it against [20].

edit.before: Our results here represent the first real-space imaging of this unique orbital magnetic phenomenon, and demonstrate that it is a generic feature of metallic orbital ferromagnets in rhombohedral graphene across a wide range of layer numbers, and must be accounted for in interpreting transport measurements whenever the ground state features valley imbalance.
edit.after: Building on imaging of density-driven valley reversal in magic-angle graphene [20], our results image gate-driven reversal of the magnetization of an entire device in rhombohedral graphene and show that it is a generic feature of metallic orbital ferromagnets in this system across a wide range of layer numbers, which must be accounted for in interpreting transport measurements whenever the ground state features valley imbalance.

issues.claim: Gate-driven sign change and capacitive reversal of the orbital magnetization in rhombohedral graphene.
issues.headline: Uncited transport study of gate-toggled orbital magnetism in hexalayer
issues.issue: Krötzsch et al. (arXiv:2509.24672) report non-volatile anomalous Hall hysteresis in rhombohedral hexalayer graphene that is toggled by sweeping density or displacement field, with a double sign reversal. It addresses the same gate-driven reversal in the same material family by transport and is not cited where the paper lists prior work on capacitive reversal.

evidence.quote: This phenomenon, unique to orbital magnets, has attracted attention [15–17, 19] because it allows magnetization to be reversed by purely capacitive means.
evidence.location: Capacitively driven domain reversal, second paragraph

issues.fix: Cite 2509.24672 alongside [15-17, 19] and note that the imaging here identifies the real-space mechanism behind such transport hysteresis.
